content:
chris: quick heads-up — starting a small dry-run to measure kernel-selection + queueing impact during a region drain. goal: isolate latency from kernel swaps vs. kv-cache cold misses. will run replay harness + synthetic fanout.

maria: SGTM. what's the exact config? batch windows, target qps, and which kernels to toggle?

chris: plan: two 10m runs per region. baseline kernel set A (fast-attn-v1, fp16 opt) then switch to kernel set B (sparse-kernel, q4 compatible). keep batching heuristics constant: max_batch=64, batch_timeout_ms=10. QPS ~2000 global, 50% origins in primary region.

alex: for infra: will we simulate cross-region routing failover (shift 60% traffic from primary->secondary over 30s)? need to ensure slot capacity in secondary is reserved.

chris: yes. drain scenario: start with steady state, then at t=5m initiate weighted shift (60% over 30s) + mark primary unhealthy for new requests. replay harness will inject realistic session traces (varying prefix lengths so kv-cache warm/cold matters).

jamie: add probe metrics for KV cache hit-rate per model-id and per-shard. last time we saw drop to 12% and p99 spiked. want that trend captured.

eva: add micro-profiling traces for kernel selection decisions (why runtime picked sparse vs dense): dump decisions with reason codes. put logs to s3://perf-dumps/1805123456/

simon: quick note on apples-to-apples: ensure the same quantized model binary across regions; only change kernel selector flag. otherwise we confound model variant effects.

chris: agreed. devs: run commands below on the harness node to start both runs (baseline then kernel-swap):

```
# baseline
./replay-harness --config cfg/drain_sensitivity.json --kernel-profile baseline --outdir /tmp/perf_baseline
# kernel swap
./replay-harness --config cfg/drain_sensitivity.json --kernel-profile swap_sparse --outdir /tmp/perf_swap
```

maria: will collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, gpu_util, kv_hit_pct, kernel-switch-counts, and batch-size-distribution. also capture tail latency percentiles by region.

alex: deploy-bot says deploy window open.

deploy-bot: Deployment window: ok to run non-prod load tests until 21:00 UTC. Reminder: limit to preprod clusters only.

jamie: observed regression in a previous run: swapping to sparse-kernel caused a 15% increase in p99 for short sequences (<32 tokens) despite lower avg tokens/sec. hypothesis: additional kernel dispatch overhead + cache miss pattern. we should add short/long sequence buckets.

eva: also instrument KV cache eviction rates. if region drain causes replays of same client session in new region, cold-start of kv causes double-penalty: kv fetch + kernel selection overhead. want to quantify that multiplier.

chris: good. data-product: produce a single CSV with run_tag, region, timestamp, p50,p95,p99,kv_hit,avg_batch,median_kernel_latency,gpu_util. we'll compare baseline vs swap_sparse.

maria: one more: set batching heuristic variant to "continuous-batching" for both runs to focus on kernel effect; don't enable adaptive batching.

simon: FYI I pushed a small instrumentation patch to log kernel decision time in ms (metric name: kernel_decision_ms). include that in dashboards.

chris: timeline: start baseline in 10m, run 10m, 5m cooldown, then swap run. posting results in this thread when done. anyone object?

alex: no objections. I'll monitor cluster pressure and autoscaler.

jamie: I'll watch SLO alerts — if p99 > 700ms for >2m we abort.

eva: thanks — if we see regression, next step is to try hybrid selector: prefer dense for seq<64 else sparse and re-run an A/B microtest.

chris: perfect. kicking off in 9m.

[10m later]

chris: baseline done. quick initial stats: p50 62ms, p95 210ms, p99 540ms, kv_hit 68%, avg_batch 22, gpu_util 42%. dumping full CSV to s3://perf-dumps/1805123456/baseline.csv

maria: noted. looks healthy. starting cooldown then swap run.

[25m later]

chris: swap run complete. initial stats: p50 68ms, p95 235ms, p99 720ms, kv_hit 37%, avg_batch 20, gpu_util 44%. kernel-switch-counts jumped x7 during drain window. full CSV at s3://perf-dumps/1805123456/swap.csv

jamie: kv_hit drop is big — that's likely replays hitting new shards post-failover. that explains large p99. any sign kernel_decision_ms spike?

simon: yes kernel_decision_ms median went from 2.1ms -> 4.9ms during the swap window. combined with extra kv round-trips seems plausible.

eva: calculate penalty multiplier: compare requests with kv_hit=true across both runs. my quick calc: p99 on kv_hit=true stayed ~500ms, kv_miss p99 went from 700ms -> 1100ms on swap. so kv misses amplify kernel swap cost.

chris: action items: 1) add a tiny sticky routing grace period during drain to preserve kv-locality (30s) 2) reduce kernel decision critical-path by caching selector outcomes per-model+seq-len 3) run hybrid selector microtest for short seqs.

maria: logging these. will schedule follow-up microtests and open an infra ticket for sticky routing experiment.

alex: created infra ticket #INF-2189 for sticky routing guards. linking to perf dumps.

chris: thanks team — will post the detailed CSVs + dashboards once cleaned. closing this dry-run thread but will reopen after microtests. :thumbsup:
